chapter: Ory, Mutt and New Orleans life
title: Ory's swing beating other bands on the wagons
summary: Hall recalls Ory's band in New Orleans winning street contests with a swinging rhythm, including a time with King Oliver.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I was going to ask him more about Mutt. When did you first play with him in Chicago, or did you play with him with Ory and New Orleans? In New Orleans.

Oh, yeah. Because I thought he was the greatest drummer in the world. Yeah. Because one time, when we used to play on the wagons, you know what I mean? We met King Oliver once, and hooked up, you know, on the bands, hooked up down there. And I'll never forget, he was playing his number of Simmons for Wobble.
And he went to blow so high and he missed the note. And Ory at that time, Ory used to beat all the bands in the street.
For the hair. Oh, yeah. It wasn't so much, the way he played.

See, Ory used to play swing like that. He didn't play all them fast numbers there. It's just a certain rhythm, swing he had, and everybody went crazy about it. That's where he'd be. Sometimes a guy said, look out, Ory's in the street today. It's the guy with ducking, because, you know, people would get around and hoop and holler and they didn't want that. But Ory just had that rhythm swing, the people just went for it. And Ory had a good band, too. Oh, yeah. A tough band, but just the way Ory played, that swing, the way he did, that's how he beat
